state: Recommend the consumer contract for already-checked BDD expressions. Two failures are established in exact generated callbacks: action input/result identifiers are free, and selected imported/local derive targets have no definition. Current callback arguments are(c,s) for tables and(c,s,b) for sequences. Bounded inspection context c is distinct from the authentic per-call execution context; s represents fresh fixture reads, b retains immutable prior bindings. Arbitrary authored fixture/parameter/let names can collide with ambient words, requiring checked lexical provenance rather than spelling heuristics. Required semantics include actual declared business result payloads, null versus missing/void discrimination, reset of current result on failure or void, earlier captures surviving subsequent calls, genuine refreshed record inputs, request overrides and rollback. Current CallOutcome success contains only ok:true, as stores that envelope, and canonical live invocation mappers drop results; implementation must repair those real owners, never manufacture a payload or derive input reads from unrelated fixtures. No new inspection authority may flow into invocation. Test modules are isolated from production consumers. Existing production function emitter is the shared owner for canonical derive bodies, checked named/default argument behavior and reachable private/default helpers, including await/lazy/source evaluation order. It must remain the sole implementation and keep external stdlib helpers as imports. Current suite emission omits derive declarations; importing the entry would include production registry initialization/dependencies, while current package modules do not provide derive implementations. Evaluate both choices against the same closure, collision safety, source semantics, producer/runner integration and actual execution qualification. Legal source support is required; this is a policy selection for implementation.

transport.description: Which callback transport meets the verified input/result semantics most simply?

criteria.bounded_context: Retain(c,s)/(c,s,b); add distinct read-only inspection slots c.inputs and c.result, compiler routes checked source bindings there; runner and canonical ports supply fresh inputs/real result and reset result, with collision-safe source routing.
criteria.explicit_frame: Extend callbacks with one explicit immutable observation frame argument containing inputs/result; preserve c/s/b roles, compiler routes checked bindings to frame; update compiler/runner/mappers and discriminate absent/null/reset.
criteria.scope_namespaces: Keep existing callback arities but extend s with distinct internal namespaces for fixtures/inputs/result and sequence b for captures; migrate fixture access consistently to prevent authored name collisions; join actual live/payload owners.

helper_composition.description: Which generated helper composition best closes selected derived calls without introducing unnecessary production dependencies?

criteria.reachable_emission: Record checked canonical derive targets while lowering a suite; reuse the existing production function/default emitter to materialize only reachable bodies and transitive private/default helpers within that test module. No production app initialization import.
criteria.shared_generated_module: Extract the same checked reachable callable closure into isolated generated helper modules shared by production/test consumers; test modules import only those units. Add artifact/link assembly while preserving private closure and single emitter.
criteria.production_entry_import: Expose checked callable exports from their actual generated production owner and import those from test modules, closing private/default dependencies there; handle and verify entry initialization/production dependencies instead of duplicating generated bodies.
